originalTitle: The reverse forest cannot terminate at the final blocker source
originalStatement: Every reverse-forest terminal has blocker source date ≤p−2; host 0 is not a terminal.

detailedDerivation: A C event has a<t<σ_h<p, so its y row is at mostp−2. At that recomputed y cell the smaller blocker p must occur in the strict left prefix because it is absent from the C host’s journal.

At a reverse host the unique y service precedes the unique p service. Traversing to its same-row left p source strictly reduces the physical host, and the next reverse y row is strictly earlier than the preceding p row.
Distinct y source rows give distinct same-row p cells; private p nonreuse then gives distinct p hosts. Thus no two C paths merge, and every finite descending path ends at a forward or W host.
Every terminal’s p row remains≤p−2. Col0’s unique private p service is at p−1 by the independently derived rail, so it cannot be a terminal.

The host-prefix Hall consequence counts each initial C/B domain host through its distinct strictly lower source. It allows unpaid forward D endpoints and does not prove A1. Unrestricted E-host descent is not used.
